meta.note: Locked mahjong terms. One form per language, decided once with a native speaker. A translation that renders a locked term differently is a CI failure, not a style preference. English forms are filled; all other core locales are explicitly null (untranslated) in Phase 1 — do NOT invent or machine-translate them.

bot.note: The CPU opponent. Never 'AI' — in every locale, the opponent is always called Bot.

research.status: Sourced research for Michael's approval — NOT native-speaker approval. Locked forms stay null until a native speaker decides. See ~/workspace/mahjong-prep/pung-pon-research.md.

dora.note: Bonus tile indicated by the dora indicator.

fu.note: Mini-points: the base value of a hand before han are applied.

furiten.note: Cannot win by ron: a tile you are waiting for is in your own pond.

han.note: Scoring unit (doubling unit); one han doubles the hand value.

honba.note: Repeat counter: extra hands the same dealer deals after winning.

research.note: Unlike pon/pung, the English source does not distinguish the kan call from the kan noun, and the drafts use the call form as the noun far more often (ja カン 56x vs 槓子 8x in the 96 pung keys). Kan noun forms were NOT rewritten in this track; native reviewer to rule — see research file.

pon.note: A three-of-a-kind meld (pung). English split: Pon is the riichi call; Pung is the noun used by American / MCR / Hong Kong / Taiwanese copy — see the research annotation on this entry.

riichi.note: The ready declaration (one away from winning, 1,000-point stick).
